newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: South Africa advisers say Kabila meeting "positive".
newsitem.headline: South Africa advisers say Kabila meeting "positive".

text.p: South African officials, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to advise on rebuilding the monetary system, had a "positive" meeting with President Laurent Kabila before flying home, Pretoria's ambassador said on Thursday.
Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad led the group who saw Kabila on Wednesday at the end of a two-day visit.
"They saw him for more than an hour and got a positive reception," ambassador Jan van Deventer told Reuters.
"We reaffirmed our commitment to assisting with the reconstruction of the Congo, but we haven't decided on any specific projects yet," he said.
Van Deventer said South Africa was keen to pursue possible cooperation in transport and electricity projects.
Officials from the two sides are to meet again, either in South Africa or in former Zaire, which Kabila renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Zaire, under ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko, was one of South Africa's main African trading partners.
Analysts say President Nelson Mandela is keen to nurture influence over the new rulers of Africa's third-largest country and potentially one of its richest.
The delegation included officials from the central Reserve Bank, the Development Bank of Southern Africa and the finance and trade departments.

South Africa this year launched a late diplomatic effort to broker a peaceful settlement between Mobutu and advancing rebel leader Kabila, but the talks faltered and Mobutu went into exile last month.

Various governments, mining companies and other business interests are now knocking on Kabila's door, hoping the new government will open up the underdeveloped country and revive an economy that imploded under Mobutu's 32-year misrule.
South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki was the first senior African leader to visit Kabila after he declared himself president in May.
